title: SHWCIM: A Scalable Heterogeneous Workload Computing-in-Memory Architecture
problem: SRAM-based CIM designs suffer from limited resource utilization, restricted multi-functionality, and constrained on-chip memory capacity, limiting their applicability to diverse workloads.
motivation: CIM offers energy efficiency but current designs are inflexible; coarse-grained reconfigurability can enable heterogeneous workload support while maintaining near-data-processing benefits.
method: HWCIM is an SRAM-based Computing-In-Memory core; SHWCIM integrates HWCIM with coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA) to support diverse workloads. Evaluated in SMIC 55nm process technology.
key_novelty: First scalable heterogeneous workload CIM architecture combining SRAM CIM cores with CGRA for flexible multi-functionality.
contributions: SRAM-based HWCIM core with improved efficiency metrics
CIM-capable CGRA integration for heterogeneous workloads
1.6x lower power and 2.8x higher energy efficiency versus prior CIM designs
4.1x smaller area, 105.9x speedup over CGRAs, 2-5x less energy than Nvidia A40 GPU

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.8x higher efficiency vs prior CIM, 2-5x vs A40 GPU

limitations: Specific workload types and detailed benchmarks for 'realistic workloads' not specified; generalization unclear.
primary_theme: Scalable heterogeneous Computing-in-Memory with CGRA integration
